title: Error Handling in Redux
description: Strategies for tracking, surfacing, and recovering from failures in Redux applications.

data.text: Every async action can fail. A robust Redux app surfaces those failures as **first-class state**, shows helpful UI, and lets the user retry — without crashing the page.

data.title: Three layers of error handling
data.text:
1. **Slice state** — per-feature errors (`state.auth.error`).
2. **Middleware** — global error logging and toasts.
3. **Error boundaries** — last-resort React catch-all.
Each feature slice should track its own loading and error state. With `createAsyncThunk`, the `pending`, `fulfilled`, and `rejected` actions do this for free.

data.title: User experience
data.text: Always tell the user **what** failed and **what they can do next**. Silent retries are the worst UX.

data.title: Add a global error toaster
data.description:
Add a global error middleware that:
1. Detects every `/rejected` action.
2. Extracts a human-readable message.
3. Dispatches a `showToast` action that any component can render.
4. Logs the error to `console.error`.
steps: Action types from `createAsyncThunk` always end in `/pending`, `/fulfilled`, or `/rejected`.
Avoid double-toasting when slices already handle the same error.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Track per-feature error state in slices
Use `rejectWithValue` from `createAsyncThunk` to keep error data structured
Add global middleware for cross-cutting error handling
Combine error boundaries, slices, and middleware for full coverage
Always show clear, recoverable messages to users
data.takeaway: Layered error handling keeps Redux apps resilient and user-friendly.
